name: LyondellBasell Industries N.V.
moat_justification: Scale and a U.S. Gulf Coast NGL feedstock cost advantage are real but are commodity cost-curve positions, not franchises: products are undifferentiated, margins are market-set spreads, and the edge depends on the oil-to-gas spread and Chinese capacity decisions. Technology licensing is a genuine niche; the European naphtha footprint is a structural disadvantage being exited at a loss.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 0.91 vs 3-yr median 5.83 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
one_liner: Commodity petrochemical leader, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% at $62.67 (weighted IRR 9.5%, IV@15 $36.20); it would need ~$36 to clear 15% on the weighted path.
moat_for: U.S. Gulf Coast NGL feedstock cost advantage vs naphtha-based rivals
Global scale and vertical integration from olefins through polymers
Technology licensing and catalyst business (differentiated, higher-margin)
Advanced Polymer Solutions specialty compounding mix
Cash conversion and cost discipline through the trough (Cash Improvement Plan)
moat_against: Commodity products with no pricing power — margins are market-set spreads
Chinese capacity additions depressing global polyethylene/polypropylene margins
European naphtha-based footprint structurally high-cost, exited at a loss
NGL advantage narrows when oil falls relative to gas
Plastics regulation (single-use bans, recycled content) caps terminal growth
